title: Kill Director Nikhil Nagesh Bhat Lands Hollywood Debut With Jamie Foxx Action Thriller
excerpt: The Indian filmmaker behind the acclaimed action hit Kill will direct Deadlocked, a courthouse siege thriller starring the Oscar winner, for Amazon's Prime Video.
body:
• Nikhil Nagesh Bhat, director of the Indian action hit Kill, will make his Hollywood debut directing Deadlocked for Amazon MGM Studios
  • Oscar winner Jamie Foxx will star as a grieving former Marine caught in a courthouse hostage situation
  • The film will stream globally on Prime Video, with a screenplay by Eric Scot Anderson and Matt Takejiro Bosack
  • Bhat's Kill premiered at TIFF, grossed over ₹47 crore, and was previously acquired by Lionsgate for a Hollywood remake

Nikhil Nagesh Bhat, the Indian filmmaker who turned heads globally with the hyper-violent action thriller Kill, has landed his first English-language feature film: a courthouse siege action thriller starring Academy Award winner Jamie Foxx, Deadline reported on Tuesday.

The film, titled Deadlocked, has been set up at Amazon MGM Studios for worldwide distribution on Prime Video. It follows a grieving former Marine serving jury duty who is forced back into action when the trial of the century turns into a deadly hostage situation after the defendant's daughter seizes the courthouse to free her father.

From Mumbai Trains to Hollywood Courthouses

Bhat gained international recognition with Kill, a relentlessly violent action film set aboard an Indian train that premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival's Midnight Madness section in September 2023. The film, starring Lakshya and Raghav Juyal, drew comparisons to the John Wick franchise for its sustained, visceral combat sequences — a comparison that proved commercially prophetic.

Lionsgate and 87Eleven Entertainment, the production company behind John Wick, acquired Kill for a mid-seven-figure deal and announced plans for an English-language remake to be produced by Chad Stahelski. Kill went on to gross over ₹47 crore at the Indian box office against a ₹40 crore budget and won six Filmfare Awards, including Best Male Debut for Lakshya.

"One of the most vivid, wild, and creative action movies I've seen recently."

— Chad Stahelski, John Wick producer, on Kill

Foxx Returns to Action

For Jamie Foxx, Deadlocked represents his latest action vehicle after the 2025 Netflix hit Back in Action, co-starring Cameron Diaz, which recorded 46.8 million views in its opening weekend. Foxx's participation is notable given his recovery from a brain bleed and stroke that forced him to leave the Back in Action shoot in 2023. His next project is Fight for '84, an Olympic boxing drama for Netflix.

The Deadlocked screenplay comes from Eric Scot Anderson (The Black Fox) and Matt Takejiro Bosack, creator of NCIS: Hawai'i. Producers include Brian Kavanaugh-Jones and Fred Berger for Range Media Partners, Dave Caplan for C2 Motion Picture Group, and Foxx through his Foxxhole Productions. Corinne Foxx, AJ Bourscheid, Liz Destro, and Paul Currie will executive produce.

Indian Directors in Hollywood

Bhat's crossover to Hollywood adds to a growing list of Indian filmmakers making inroads into the global mainstream. S.S. Rajamouli's RRR broke through with audiences worldwide and won an Academy Award for Best Original Song. Bhat had earlier been reported to be developing a project with Universal Studios, according to Bollywood Hungama, though it appears the Amazon deal materialised first.

Beyond Kill, Bhat's filmography includes the thriller Apurva, the drama Hurdang, and the web series Rasbhari and The Gone Game. He was reportedly attached to Parshuram, an action thriller starring Sunny Deol, though that project's status is uncertain following the Deadlocked announcement.

What's Next

No release date has been announced for Deadlocked, which has not yet begun filming. Based on typical production timelines, the earliest window would be summer 2027. For Indian cinema fans, the pairing of Bhat's kinetic action sensibility with Foxx's star power and Amazon's global distribution muscle makes this one of the more intriguing crossover projects in recent memory.
